scope: Proposition 4.5 (Uniform local counts and conditional fields) of the manuscript “Uniform excess charge for Coulomb molecules and the outer radius of neutral atoms” (preprints/Uniform-excess-charge-for-Coulomb-molecules-and-the-outer-radius-of-neutral-atoms-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 263 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5abedb3de1f8ed28), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In either geometry, every normal- ized δ-state in a finite sector satisfies P ≤ C. Fix y ∈ Y. Suppose the initial finite sequence of cuts has total out support covered by at most C0 cells Bz, with C−1 0 ≤ az/ay ≤ C0, and satisfies the gradient hypothesis of Lemma 4.2. The absent-cut case is allowed. Then P ≤ C, ⃦ ⃦(E[Jy | X])+ ⃦ ⃦ 2 ≤ C(C0) my ay . (4.39) Neither constant depends on the nuclear system, particle number, state, target, or δ.
